KeysToEntries.TravelingScavenger_01:
Entry 1:

Barely slept last night. Found an old shed to hide in, but the wind was so strong it felt like the whole place might collapse. Moved out at first light, sticking to the edge of the desert. Came across a wrecked service station. Most of it was looted, but I found some expired meds and a small solar-powered radio. The skies have been an unnatural shade of orange, and the air's heavy with dust—feels like a storm's coming, but it's hard to tell anymore.
KeysToEntries.TravelingScavenger_02:
Entry 2:

Stumbled upon a small campfire, still smoldering. Someone's close, but I didn't stick around. I'm rationing the last of the protein bars I found in a smashed vending machine. On the bright side, my radio finally picked up a faint signal—some automated distress call on a loop, but I can't make any sense of it. I think maybe it's old, probably from before everything fell apart, but it's a grim reminder.
KeysToEntries.TravelingScavenger_03:
Entry 3:

Crossed paths with a wild dog today. We stared at each other before it darted off. I was tempted to follow, hoping it knew where to find food, I lost track of it in the brush. Found a nearly dry creek in the shrublands and filled up anything I could with fresh water. I thought I heard a strange buzzing overhead, but it was hard to make out over the flowing stream. I didn't wait around.
KeysToEntries.TravelingScavenger_04:
Entry 4:

Narrowly avoided a group of scavengers today. They had strange clothing adorned with tech I didn't recognize. I hid in the underbrush until they left. Saw one of them using some kind of handheld device to scan the area; it beeped once, then went silent. They moved on, but it's clear they're better equipped than I am. Found some freeze-dried food in a hidden cache. It's old but still edible. I'll keep moving, avoiding any encounters if I can.
KeysToEntries.TravelingScavenger_05:
Entry 5:

Found a deserted warehouse on the outskirts of shrublands. It's been stripped of anything valuable, but I found some canned food hidden in one of the shipping containers. I kept hearing a metalic tapping sound as I moved around the building. Birds in the rafters? The skies have a reddish tint, probably from distant wildfires. Even here, the air smells faintly of smoke. The weather's unpredictable—searing heat one day, freezing winds the next, it's exhausting.
KeysToEntries.TravelingScavenger_06:
Entry 6:

Stumbled into an overgrown forest today. The dense foliage offered good cover, but the air is humid and thick with pollen. I wrapped my face in cloth. The climate's gone haywire; everything feels alien. Followed a stream, hoping it might lead somewhere, but it just wound deeper into the woods. Found an old hunting trap—rusty but still functional. Ate the last of my food today. The humidity is suffocating, and I can't shake the feeling of being watched.
KeysToEntries.TravelingScavenger_07:
Entry 7:

Tried to raid an old apartment block on the edge of a swamp, but it was a bust—everything picked clean. Almost got caught by a couple of scavengers who were moving through the area. Hid in a drainage tunnel until they left. I found a bag someone left behind, a small electric device was the only thing left inside. I have no idea what it actually does, but I know a grenade when I see one.


There's a huge dam across the swamp, a hole blown clean through the center of it. I can't see what's on the other side from here.
KeysToEntries.TravelingScavenger_08:
Entry 8:

Crossed part of the swamp today, small paths and bridges barely holding together. Found some emergency rations in an old vehicle—they were vacuum-sealed, so still good. The terrain's getting rougher, there's moss and vines growing in huge patches. The storms lately have been terrifying—lightning strikes everywhere, with no rain, just dry heat. My shoes are falling apart, but I haven't found anything better. Staying on foot is wearing me down, but stopping isn't an option.
KeysToEntries.TravelingScavenger_09:
Entry 9:

I made it to one half of the dam, completely deserted inside. The air smelled faintly of chemicals; I kept my face wrapped in cloth. I heard it again, the buzzing overhead as I moved through an old generator hall. I hid among some machinery and I saw it—a drone passing above a skylight. Is it the government? Is it lost?

The sky is choked with ash from distant wildfires, it was hard to make out and passed by before I could get a better look.
KeysToEntries.TravelingScavenger_10:
Entry 10:

Saw smoke on the horizon this morning—possibly from a campfire or more wildfires. Found a small solar-powered flashlight in half-buried in the mud; it still works. The nights are longer now, and the temperature swings are brutal—scorching during the day, freezing at night. It's like the climate's lost all sense of balance. I need to keep moving, staying sharp. The air's too thick to breathe without a filter. A drone passed overhead again, this time closer. I'm starting to think it's not just lost—it's looking.
KeysToEntries.TravelingScavenger_11:
Entry 11:

The road's been quiet for days. I've been moving through dense overgrown forests, following faint signals on my radio. Found some wild berries—they tasted strange but didn't make me sick. No signs of people, which is both a blessing and a curse. The weather's so unpredictable that I've been drenched in sweat one moment, freezing the next. I'm trying to stay off the obvious paths, but my gear's wearing out, and every step feels heavier.
KeysToEntries.TravelingScavenger_12:
Entry 12:

Came across a group of deer in the foothills today. They didn't seem too bothered by me, which was a relief. I tried to catch one, but I'm no hunter. The air was heavy with fog, making it hard to see more than a few meters. Found an old stash of supplies in an abandoned cabin. Most of the things are broken, but I might be able to salvage some parts. Ate the last of my food. The climate's gotten so extreme it's hard to predict what the next day will bring.
KeysToEntries.TravelingScavenger_13:
Entry 13:

Almost got caught in a brutal rainstorm today—came out of nowhere. The wind howled, visibility was zero, so I found shelter in an old shipping container I nearly ran into. Inside, it was dark but safe. Someone had been here before me, it was cleaned out except for some plastic bottles. The storm lasted hours, maybe longer; hard to tell time in there. When it finally cleared, everything was covered in mud and debris. The landscape's completely changed.
KeysToEntries.TravelingScavenger_14:
Entry 14:

The weather's been strange lately—unseasonable cold in the middle of what should be summer. Found an old pair of binoculars in a deserted factory near the swamps. It'll be nice to scout from a distance instead of always walking into trouble. I saw more drones today, near the horizon. I almost mistook them for birds. Moving further towards the mountains might be my only option.
KeysToEntries.TravelingScavenger_15:
Entry 15:

Barely escaped a flash flood while foraging in the swamp today. The rain came out of nowhere, turning the low pools into a rushing river within minutes. Managed to climb onto an overturned bus for safety. The water was filthy, filled with debris. The floodwaters are receding, but everything's soaked. Found some dry clothes in the bus—too big, but better than nothing. I need to be more careful.
KeysToEntries.TravelingScavenger_16:
Entry 16:

Encountered a massive hailstorm in the overgrown forest—chunks of ice the size of golf balls. Took cover in a cave, but the entrance was partially blocked by fallen rocks. Managed to squeeze inside and wait out the storm. Found some graffiti on the cave wall—a giant mural of some sort but I couldn't tell what it meant. It's clear this place has seen others like me. I'll push further towards the mountains tomorrow. I've heard the buzzing more often now, and other sounds I don't recognize. I'm not sure I should stay around here much longer.
KeysToEntries.TravelingScavenger_17:
Entry 17:

The drone sightings have increased lately. They're not just passing by—they're actively patrolling. I've seen them more frequently closer to the dam, and it's clear they're monitoring the area. Found an old communications tower and tried to find anything useful, but there's no power. I've watched the drones from a distance—they're familiar and foreign at the same time. I've had to take extra care not to get detected, they're more acute than the seem. I think they're armed.
KeysToEntries.TravelingScavenger_18:
Entry 18:

The situation with the drones has gotten worse. They're becoming more aggressive, almost like they're hunting for something—or someone. I tried to avoid them, but one almost spotted me while I was scavenging in an out-building near the dam. I have the electronic grenade-thing, but I still have no idea what it does. I need to stay out of their line of sight and find a secure place to hide. If I have to compete with other scavengers and avoid these drones, I'm worried about my prospects.
KeysToEntries.TravelingScavenger_19:
Entry 19:

The drones are relentless now. They seem to follow a pattern, but it's erratic and hard to predict. Today, I watched from a safe distance as they engaged with a group of scavengers—firing warning shots and harassing them. I'm starting to think these drones are not just surveillance but actively enforcing some sort of control. I'll stay hidden and try to figure out what they're up to. The weather has normalized somewhat so at least there's that.
KeysToEntries.TravelingScavenger_20:
Entry 20:

Hiked to the other side of the dam and found an old research station. The drones are definitely watching over this area, as evidenced by the frequent patrols. Managed to get inside the station and found a cache of supplies—food, blankets, and a better radio. The patrols make it hard to stay hidden, but the research station's more defensible than a bus in the woods. The drones are getting more aggressive, and I need to stay alert to avoid them.
KeysToEntries.TravelingScavenger_21:
Entry 21:

The drones are no longer just a nuisance—they're a danger. New kinds have been showing up—a lot bigger than the others. I've found some old maps in the research center and it looks like there's some kind of tunnel at the south end of the valley. I'm going to set out in in the morning.

I think my time here has come to an end.
